feedback.label: Health crowding, freshness/Refresh grouping, activity hierarchy
feedback.disposition: Health is one left-aligned 42rem reading column: a grouped observation block, fixed-order 44px issue rows with subordinate per-issue help, adjacent stale and unavailable notices, and a subordinate Recent activity section. The composition was chosen by a bounded 252-measurement comparison (Winner A) and is held by population, geometry, axe, link-landing and focus gates. Stories prove rendering only; every issue link is proven on the real route.

feedback.label: Preview reset alignment/weight and repetitive helpers
feedback.disposition: Restore defaults is now a bordered, aligned action with the unchanged reset handler. The repeated generic value helpers are gone: read-only values share one note, and an all-read-only scenario shows the no-editable message with no note. A field error names the specific problem and is the only description of its control. Parsing and validation are unchanged.

feedback.label: Readable selected Preview scenario/module identity
feedback.disposition: The selector shows a humanized scenario label first, the Mailable second, and the exact Module.scenario identity as visible wrapping monospace text, with no middle-dot join. Scenarios that humanize to the same label fall back to their raw atoms, and Mailables that share a leaf are told apart by namespace. URLs are unchanged.

feedback.label: Compact Account context and coherent Preview return
feedback.disposition: The Account control heads the Health, Deliveries and Inbound group it scopes and offers a picker only when there is a real choice; Preview sits outside the group, shows no Account identity, and returns to the originating Account through a validated closed-set return context. Stories prove rendering only; scope and return are proven on the real routes and in the reference demo.

feedback.label: Auto-apply both collections, no Apply
feedback.disposition: Both live lists auto-apply: select changes and Enter commit straight to the canonical URL with no Apply control, and debounced Search edits add one history entry each. Back and Forward restore the filters with the search focused, a Clear during a pending debounce ends cleared, and a failed read shows an error with Retry rather than an empty population. FILTER-01 through FILTER-04 are connected-only, so there is no Storybook scenario; the cases run on the real routes in mailglass_admin/e2e/phase176-filters.spec.js.

feedback.label: Quiet quick-view arrows on both surfaces
feedback.disposition: Enabled navigation uses unoutlined 44px ghost-arrow links with accessible names, visible hover and focus states, and readable position. At Delivery boundaries the unavailable control is a generic inert span with screen-reader text and no link/button semantics; Inbound keeps its native disabled button. The two adapters retain their intended, different boundary semantics. Connected evidence: reference/demo_app/assets/e2e/quick-views.spec.js and phase173-evidence.spec.js cover tracer, Delivery and Inbound cases; the 320/375/768/1280/1440 light/dark matrix and exact current Axe report are indexed in mailglass_admin/docs/phase174-review.md. Routes: /ops/mail?tenant_id=northstar&view=deliveries and /ops/mail/inbound?tenant_id=northstar&provider=postmark&window_hours=168. Retained production stories: /dev/storybook/quick_views/delivery and /dev/storybook/quick_views/inbound.

feedback.label: Raw provider source hierarchy and privacy/reveal grouping
feedback.disposition: The production EvidenceCard groups the raw source heading, reveal control and privacy copy with compact facts, and one source selector drives both byte size and the revealed text. Reveal stays authorization-gated and shows only the safe source allowlist; unknown, empty-revealed, large-revealed and denied evidence are each rendered truthfully, and denial is announced rather than shown as zero. Stories prove rendering only; reveal and denial are proven on the real route.

feedback.label: Suppression Refresh/Retry and truthful wording
feedback.disposition: Account-scoped Refresh uses a real retry and preserves retained evidence as stale on failure; unavailable evidence and unknown expiry remain distinct, and unknown expiry is not described as permanent.

feedback.label: Complete ordinary authorized Inbound addresses
feedback.disposition: Ordinary authorized contacts show complete addresses: long local parts, Unicode, spoofed display names, many recipients, missing headers and unparseable headers all render through the production DetailHeader, with the envelope recipient kept distinct from header contacts. The visible address is also in the accessible name. Raw source, routing/header/matcher diagnostics, telemetry and logs stay separately protected.

feedback.label: Storybook navigation, fonts/themes/hooks and stories beyond primitives

current_sources.symbol: MailglassDemoWeb.Storybook.js_body/0 (production hook registration and story-local Light/Dark/System adapter)

feedback.disposition: The generated root, Theme Picker, sidebar, direct story, internal assets, and retained production Delivery/Inbound quick views work under /dev/storybook. Fresh cold/warm evidence covers exact production CSS and loaded font faces, story-owned Light/Dark/System behavior under live OS changes, real iframe hook registration/mount/remove/remount and route cycles, and the strict 18-case Admin Axe comparison. The scan has zero violations and zero untriaged findings; its 50 incomplete findings remain explicit and are not claimed as passes. Phase 178 closed the two remaining items. The serif StatCard feedback has a computed font-role receipt: the demo case 'Phase 178 StatCard story uses the production font roles' in reference/demo_app/assets/e2e/phase178-stories.spec.js compares the label, value and UI roles of the light and dark StatCard stories with the same component rendered by the production Admin gallery from the same CSS bytes, and asserts no serif fallback and loaded production faces. Real browser zoom is covered by the five Phase 178 real-zoom cases in mailglass_admin/e2e/phase178-real-zoom.spec.js (Delivery and Inbound quick views, Health, Account, and the Deliveries and Inbound filters at 320 CSS px under actual 200% tab zoom) and by the extended Phase 171 actual-zoom case for Preview Restore defaults and the technical identity line. The reproduction commands and receipts are in 178-AUTOMATION.md. Current stories: /dev/storybook, /dev/storybook/primitives/theme_picker, /dev/storybook/primitives/stat_card, /dev/storybook/quick_views/delivery, /dev/storybook/quick_views/inbound, /dev/storybook/assets.

feedback.label: Quick-view replay, truthful availability, concise dialog/X, success toast and inline errors/retry
feedback.disposition: Exact target, no-fallback, permitted/unavailable/ambiguous/denied/failed outcomes, shared dialog keyboard/focus behavior, visible failure recovery, accessible success toast, and durable actual audit outcome are covered. Provider delivery is not claimed.

feedback.label: Technical evidence visible by default on full detail
feedback.disposition: Grouped Delivery and Inbound full-detail technical fields are visible without expansion. Current connected-route assertions verify exact identity, bounded values, and no horizontal overflow; compact quick-view technical details remain a distinct presentation.
